1	# Roster
2	
3	> Roster is an agent that runs performance reviews for your AI coding agents.
4	
5	It reads every session your coding agents recorded with [Entire](https://entire.io), and for each one works out:
6	- what it cost
7	- whether its change survived
8	- whether it was reverted, or reworked by a person
9	
10	Then it tests a better setup on your own past tasks, and ships that setup only if nothing regresses.
11	
12	**Live:**
13	- [roster-five-chi.vercel.app](https://roster-five-chi.vercel.app)
14	- [our own AI team's review](https://roster-five-chi.vercel.app/r/rajkaria/roster)
15	- [all reviews](https://roster-five-chi.vercel.app/r)
16	
17	## What it does
18	
19	A **setup** is a coding-agent harness, a model and a rules file, for example Claude Code with Sonnet 5.5 and your `CLAUDE.md`. Roster:
20	
21	1. **Reviews:** it scores every recorded session of every setup.
22	   - It prices the session from its tokens.
23	   - It checks whether its lines survived at `HEAD`, were reverted, or were reworked by a person.
24	   - It checks whether the session ran unattended.
25	   - Setups are compared on tasks of similar difficulty (Mantel–Haenszel across difficulty terciles). This is **evidence level A, observational**: it can name a suspect but proves nothing on its own.
26	2. **Replays:** it reruns a setup's real past tasks at their parent commit, in a sandbox with no future history.
27	   - Each task runs under the incumbent setup and under candidate setups.
28	   - Each attempt is graded with the tests the team kept, the full suite, a scope guard and a blind diff judge.
29	   - **Level B.**
30	3. **Gates:** a deterministic gate promotes a candidate only if nothing regresses. The model decides what to try next, and the gate decides what ships.
31	4. **Tests forward:** new tasks, written and hashed before the decision, run through the old and the new setup side by side and are graded blind. **Level C.**
32	5. **Books:** it writes the AI team's spend per setup into the company's [cfo.ai](https://cfo.ai) plan, with a hire-or-scale scenario. *(Pending: needs the cfo.ai connection.)*
33	
34	Every Roster run is traced in [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com).
35	
36	## This repo is the experiment
37	
38	Four coding-agent setups built this repo, assigned to tasks by a seeded shuffle and recorded by Entire ([`setups/`](setups)):
39	
40	| Setup | Harness | Model | Rules |
41	|---|---|---|---|
42	| A | Claude Code | Opus 5.5 | default |
43	| B | Claude Code | Sonnet 5.5 | default |
44	| C | Claude Code | Haiku 5.5 | default |
45	| D | Claude Code | Sonnet 5.5 | default + strict |
46	
47	The candidates run Claude Code on DeepSeek:
48	
49	| Candidate | Model |
50	|---|---|
51	| E | DeepSeek Flash |
52	| F | DeepSeek V4 Pro |
53	
54	The test was fixed in advance in [`experiments/PREREGISTRATION.md`](experiments/PREREGISTRATION.md):
55	- The 40 forward tasks and their acceptance tests were frozen before the first review. The hashes are in [`experiments/FREEZE.txt`](experiments/FREEZE.txt).
56	- Every change since then is a dated amendment, including two protocol deviations and the first review's weak evidence.
57	
58	**Status, from [`docs/FACTS.md`](docs/FACTS.md):**
59	- **Level A:** Roster reviewed its own repo (61 sessions, 4 setups) and found **no suspect** (odds ratio 4.23, p = 1.000).
60	- **Level B:** Review 1 promoted **E** over B. The two tied at zero hidden-test passes, and E was cheaper. That is weak evidence, and amendment 7 says so: even the incumbent failed its own replayed tasks. The replay bug behind it is being fixed.
61	- **Level C:** the forward run of B against E is in progress. Results will be published whatever they show.
62	
63	## Roster caught its own silent mistakes
64	
65	Reviewing its own build, Roster's v1 output was green but wrong six times. Each was fixed by a recorded agent task:
66	- It saw 3 setups where there were 4.
67	- It priced Haiku sessions at $0.
68	- It dropped the hidden tests of 16 of 23 tasks.
69	- It counted one prompt as three.
70	- Its replays failed without a reason.
71	- It priced DeepSeek runs at Claude rates.
72	
73	The build log in [`hackathon.md`](hackathon.md) has the details.
74	
75	## Run it
76	
77	```bash
78	bun install
79	bun src/cli.ts review https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> --observational   # level A, read-only, no model calls
80	bun src/cli.ts run <repo> --budget 5                                        # coordinator: plan, replay, gate (DeepSeek)
81	bun src/cli.ts forward --backlog <file> --pair OLD,NEW                      # paired forward run, blind grading
82	```
83	
84	**Requirements:**
85	- The repo must record sessions with Entire (`entire/checkpoints/v1` or `refs/entire/checkpoints/*`).
86	- Replays need the Claude Code CLI.
87	- Roster's own reasoning uses DeepSeek: set `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in `.env`.
88	
89	[`docs/DESIGN.md`](docs/DESIGN.md) is the engineering contract.
90	
91	## Built with
92	
93	| Tool | What it does in Roster |
94	|---|---|
95	| **Entire** | The data Roster reads (sessions, prompts, tokens, model, commit), and the recorder for every session that built Roster |
96	| **neatlogs** | Traces every Roster run, from ingest to each replay attempt and gate decision |
97	| **cfo.ai** | Where Roster books the AI team as a department of the company plan *(connection pending)* |
98	
99	## Limits
100	
101	- Tests are a proxy for value.
102	- Level A on a young repo is mostly "insufficient data" or "no suspect", by design.
103	- Replays of public repos must run in isolated VMs; local replays are only for repos you trust.
104	
105	## License
106	
107	MIT
